MC	<p>09e1_604a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03421;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a03421;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03421;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #24701b;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #24701b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #24701b;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6546b1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fpt, +++, fpt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d809_9709</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hnp, +++, hnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4ab4_e0e5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #0d6787;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, adm, +++, adm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6cd0_6e99</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9f2e4f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ckn, +++, ckn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>930a_d6e2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, efk, +++, efk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03421;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a03421;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03421;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bcp, +++, bcp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5c85_81ea</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596519;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #596519;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596519;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, akw, +++, akw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d3e4_515d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #0d6787;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bpw, +++, bpw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7f97_68b3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6546b1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aex, +++, aex"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6546b1;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, afn, +++, afn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>74f9_2a06</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6546b1;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cey, +++, cey"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03421;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a03421;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03421;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #24701b;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #24701b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #24701b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6546b1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hnx, +++, hnx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03421;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a03421;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03421;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #24701b;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #24701b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #24701b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>81f8_1a6a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mwx, +++, mwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b474_0a10</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596519;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #596519;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596519;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6546b1;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfr, +++, cfr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>df2a_c743</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #0d6787;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hjx, +++, hjx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>94c9_f583</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cew, +++, cew"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6b08_37f7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, adf, +++, adf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d673_171e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9f2e4f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bde, +++, bde"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>675a_25f9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cmp, +++, cmp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #24701b;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #24701b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #24701b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #0d6787;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>8524_2a4a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8d4914;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8d4914;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d4914;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ckp, +++, ckp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>335b_1405</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8d4914;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8d4914;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d4914;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cjm, +++, cjm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e816_ded5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fpw, +++, fpw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0da5_ee11</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cty, +++, cty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4726_30e8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, pxy, +++, pxy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>643c_7bec</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9f2e4f;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kmw, +++, kmw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a896_099c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f2e4f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fkn, +++, fkn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d714_2172</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0d6787;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, krx, +++, krx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>544d_6c91</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03421;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a03421;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03421;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #24701b;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #24701b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #24701b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cep, +++, cep"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>074f_338f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #24701b;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #24701b;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #24701b;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ajy, +++, ajy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #24701b;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #24701b;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #24701b;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f2e4f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jkm, +++, jkm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>364a_7565</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596519;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #596519;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596519;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6546b1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bpt, +++, bpt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d368_6274</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bfy, +++, bfy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a622_3e72</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #24701b;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #24701b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #24701b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #0d6787;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9f2e4f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhm, +++, bhm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8b77_dea1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03421;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a03421;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03421;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6546b1;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, axy, +++, axy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b47c_9ed7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, prt, +++, prt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>02a4_fcac</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6e5d00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f2e4f;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, krx, +++, krx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>fd33_a0a4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9f2e4f;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8d4914;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8d4914;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d4914;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aky, +++, aky"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9a99_9434</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dfm, +++, dfm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03421;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a03421;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03421;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6546b1;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6546b1;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>7bcb_22dc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2c6195;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6195;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, axy, +++, axy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9f17_18f8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03421;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a03421;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03421;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d64;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006d64;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d64;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, efw, +++, efw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9989_1076</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8d4914;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8d4914;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d4914;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mtx, +++, mtx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
