MC	<p>e3bd_5b30</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bkt, +++, bkt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3a6c_a8aa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7f5400;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5400;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abp, +++, abp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>24d8_094b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #24701b;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #24701b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #24701b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #0d6787;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0d6787;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7f3c99;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3c99;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bjw, +++, bjw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e513_bb66</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596519;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #596519;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596519;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8d3a75;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a75;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bnp, +++, bnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #196e4d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #196e4d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4056b0;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4056b0;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f2e4f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2e4f;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, axy, +++, axy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
